Hi Helen / Ben —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of the ask (as I heard it)
- You will be sending prompts and receiving model-generated outputs from Redwood-hosted endpoints.
- Primary requirement: no long-term storage of any PII derived from prompts or model outputs without explicit written consent.
- Data residency: production inference and logs must be pinned to US regions only (us-east-1 preferred).
- Retention windows: you asked for maximum retention of raw logs for 90 days, but are okay with short debug windows if necessary for incident investigation.

Open items we promised to confirm:
1) Exactly what we persist by default (prompts, outputs, embeddings, traces) and retention periods.
2) Whether we can restrict residency to a single US region and provide a signed DPA/KMS controls.
3) Whether there are opt-out or configuration flags for suppressing storage of prompt text and outputs.

Attachments: SOC2 summary and a DPA draft are attached for your review (see files). I also attached a retention matrix with our current defaults for hosting.

Proposed immediate next steps
- I will get an authoritative confirmation from our security/product team on the exact storage/retention semantics (aiming for EOD tomorrow).
- If the answers match your requirements, we can exchange a redlined DPA and schedule a 30-min legal/infosec call next week to sign off.

If I missed anything in the recap, call it out and I will update.

Cheers,

Hi Helen / Ben —

Thanks for the questions — below are the canonical behaviors and the toggles/options we can provide. I copied Tessa, Marcus and Monica to surface any implementation/ops notes.

1) Default persistence of prompts and outputs- Hosted API (default configuration): prompts and model outputs are NOT written to customer-visible long-term storage by default. We retain short-term debug logs (rotating) for operational troubleshooting for up to 7 days; these are accessible only to authorized ops/security personnel and are encrypted at rest. After 7 days, raw logs are purged and only aggregated telemetry (token counts, error rates, latencies) is retained for 90 days.

2) Embeddings- Embeddings are NOT stored by default unless the customer enables persistent embeddings storage via the API (this is an explicit opt-in configuration). If enabled, embeddings are stored encrypted and can be pinned to a region; retention is customer-configurable.

3) Opt-out / storage suppression- We support a "no-store" configuration for hosted customers where prompts/outputs are never persisted beyond in-memory buffers used for inference. This mode disables long-term logs and persistent embeddings and is fully supported, though it disables features that rely on persisted text (e.g., query history, certain debugging traces).

4) Data residency- We can pin inference processing, backup snapshots, and logs to a single US region (us-east-1). This is available for customers on an enterprise plan (we document this option in the DPA).

5) KMS / encryption- Customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) are supported for encryption-at-rest on persisted artifacts (logs, snapshots, embeddings) when the customer requests them; we will include the KMS configuration section in the DPA.

6) Additional controls and evidence- Attached are our SOC2 summary and an internal retention matrix showing default windows and the "no-store" option. We can provide a data-processing addendum (DPA) with the specific language you need; please review the attached DPA draft and propose redlines.

Next steps
- Tessa: share this text with Nimbus legal/infosec and confirm whether the "no-store" mode or the pinned-us-east-1 option is preferred.
- If Nimbus wants pinned residency + KMS, we’ll route to engineering to scope the onboarding (usually 5–10 business days for region pin + KMS config).

If you want me to join the call with your infosec/legal, happy to — just let us know a time.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Staff Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
